prompt:
Scene:
A square photograph at humid late afternoon, 28mm full-frame camera deep inside a tropical rainforest. Dense canopy layers filter sunlight into moving green shafts; high humidity visible as thick air haze between the trees.

Subject:
A three-tiered jungle waterfall where every tier has reversed. Water leaves a pool at the forest floor, climbs over the first ledge in a 15-meter reverse cascade, then the second, then the third, before disappearing into the canopy above and resurfacing as mist between leaves. Ferns and moss-covered rocks around the pool are saturated with the upward splash-back.

Important details:
Tropical photorealism: glossy wet leaves, rich moss, occasional tropical flower. The reverse cascades retain real fluid detail — foam at each ledge, individual droplet trails rising. A small parrot lands on a moss-covered branch; a tree frog sits on a reverse-dripping leaf. Moisture haze catches light shafts vertically, reinforcing the upward read.

Use case:
Lift-studies single 5/5 — tropical biome reverse-cascade three-tier study.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no branded tourist gear, no Mayan ruins, no cartoon, no stylized illustration.
